# Service Beacon bench plan and virtual bench

**Generated by** `tools/generate_model_docs.py`. **No hardware exists.** Expected values come from the engineering model (`ios.evaluate_beacon_engineering_budget`, built on *assumed* derating, radio and battery figures); the virtual bench uses *assumed* component tolerances. It prepares milestone M3 (bench demonstration) and BEACON-01; it does not satisfy it.

## 1. Survival sizing (Guide §15: E_usable ≥ P_avg × T_survival)

Guide worked example reproduced by `bench.average_power_w`: 0.01 W sleep + 1 % × 2 W TX + 10 % × 0.03 W sensing = **0.033 W**, 30 days = **23.76 Wh** ideal. The model beacon (1 Hz, 15 ms TX) draws **28.5 mW**; derated nameplate for 30 days is **49.2 Wh** (derating 0.50: converter, isolation, −20 °C, 15-year aging, depth of discharge, +20 % margin).

## 2. Periodic pulses vs wake-on-command (30 days)

| Mode | Avg power mW | Energy Wh | Time to first data s | Note |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|:--|
| periodic | 28.5 | 20.5 | 1 | broadcasts without being asked; also helps a servicer find the client |
| wake_on_command | 12.5 | 9.0 | 6 | needs the servicer to know when/where to interrogate; adds spoofing/authentication surface |

Wake-on-command saves energy (assumes 18 mW receiver at 2 % duty and 10 minutes of interrogation per day) but depends on the servicer finding and interrogating the client, and adds an authentication surface. Periodic pulses are the safer default for a client that may be tumbling and silent.

## 3. Antenna coverage under tumble

For a randomly oriented client with two opposite patch antennas of half-beamwidth θ, P(servicer inside a cone) = 2 × (1 − cos θ) / 2. Packets needed for ≥ 1 reception at 95 % confidence:

| Patch half-angle | P(cover) | Packets at 0 % loss | At 50 % loss | At 75 % loss |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 45° | 0.29 | 9 | 19 | 40 |
| 60° | 0.50 | 5 | 11 | 23 |
| 75° | 0.74 | 3 | 7 | 15 |
| 90° | 1.00 | 1 | 5 | 11 |

At 1 Hz a 45° patch pair needs about 9 packets (9 s) with no loss and about 40 s at 75 % loss, so first contact is not the binding constraint; rate quality is. Packets are treated as independent; real patterns, body blockage and the correlation of orientation between consecutive packets are not modelled.

## 4. Bench tests (expected values and pass limits from the model)

| ID | Test | Measure | Expected | Pass limit | Procedure |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|--:|:--|
| B1 | Sleep + duty-cycled average power | average input power over 1 h at 1 Hz, nominal temp | 28.5 mW | ≤ 35.6 mW | Power from a 3.6 V source through a precision shunt; log 1 h; TX 15 ms at 1 Hz |
| B2 | Main-bus short isolation leakage | reserve-cell drain with main bus shorted to 0 ohm | 2.0 uA | ≤ 10.0 uA | Short the main-bus input; measure reserve draw; repeat with over-voltage step to 1.25x nominal |
| B3 | Transmit power at antenna port | RF power at 401.5 MHz | 27.0 dBm | ≥ 25.0 dBm | Spectrum analyser through calibrated attenuator |
| B4 | Link margin at 1 km equivalent | Eb/N0 margin with attenuator emulating free-space loss + tumble gain -3 dBi | 55.0 dB | ≥ 10.0 dB | Attenuator set to FSPL(1 km)=84.5 dB; PRBS; measure BER <= 1e-5 |
| B5 | Cold usable capacity | capacity delivered to cutoff at -20 C vs nameplate | 41.8 Wh | ≥ 34.9 Wh | Thermal chamber -20 C; constant-power discharge at the average load |
| B6 | Packet timestamp / latency | timestamp to RX latency jitter | 50.0 ms | ≤ 250.0 ms | Loop-back with GPS-disciplined clock; 10,000 packets |
| B7 | Replay / spoof rejection | fraction of replayed or bad-token commands rejected | 100.0 % | ≥ 100.0 % | Inject 1,000 replayed and 1,000 bad-token commands; zero may be accepted |

Record measured values and call `bench.evaluate_bench({'B1': ..., ...})` to get PASS / FAIL / NOT_RUN per test.

## 5. Virtual bench (20,000 sampled builds)

Component spreads are assumptions: sleep power ±25 % (1σ lognormal), TX power ±12 %, leakage ±50 %, RF output ±0.8 dB, link ±2.5 dB, cold capacity factor 0.85 ± 0.04, latency jitter 50 ± 40 ms.

| ID | Test | P(pass) | 5th pct | 95th pct |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| B1 | Sleep + duty-cycled average power | 95.1% | 23.5 | 35.6 |
| B2 | Main-bus short isolation leakage | 99.9% | 0.9 | 4.5 |
| B3 | Transmit power at antenna port | 99.4% | 25.7 | 28.3 |
| B4 | Link margin at 1 km equivalent | 100.0% | 50.6 | 59.3 |
| B5 | Cold usable capacity | 99.9% | 38.0 | 45.7 |
| B6 | Packet timestamp / latency | 100.0% | 5.4 | 117.3 |

B1 is the tightest (limit is only 25 % above the model average); a design review should either tighten sleep-current control or widen the energy margin. B7 (spoof rejection) is a logic test, not statistical: any acceptance is a fail.
